p: שַׁבָּת זֶה כְּשֶׁחָל בּוֹ רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ יֵשׁ בּוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ קְדוּשּׁוֹת וְהַחוּט הַמְשׁוּלָּשׁ לֹא בִמְהֵרָה יִנָּתֵק.
— When Rosh Chodesh falls on this Shabbat, it contains three sanctities, and “the threefold cord is not quickly broken.”
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא כְּבָר בְּחִינַת אֱמֶת וּכְתִיב וּשְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד,
— It thus already embodies truth, and it is written, “The lip of truth will be established forever.”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר יַעֲקֹב חֶבֶל נַחֲלָתוֹ וְאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סח) מָה הַחֶבֶל הַזֶּה פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה אֵין מַפְקִיעִין אוֹתוֹ כָּךְ הָאָבוֹת אֵין פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה.

— As it says, “Jacob is the cord of His inheritance.” The Sages explain that just as a cord is not braided from fewer than three strands, so there are no fewer than three patriarchs (Bereishit Rabbah 68).

וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב כּוֹלֵל קְדוּשַּׁת אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א׳ רז א) וְרָזָא דַּאֲבָהָן דָּא הוּא יַעֲקֹב דְּאִיהוּ כְּלָלָא דִּלְהוֹן בְּגִין דְּיַעֲקֹב תּוּשְׁבַּחְתָּא דַּאֲבָהָן אִיהוּ,
— Jacob encompasses the sanctity of Abraham and Isaac. As stated in Zohar I, 207a: “The mystery of the patriarchs is Jacob, who encompasses them, for Jacob is the glory of the patriarchs.”

וּכְתִיב תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב וּשְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר יַעֲקֹב חֶבֶל נַחֲלָתוֹ שֶׁהוּא כּוֹלֵל כָּל הַשָּׁלֹשׁ קְדוּשּׁוֹת הָאָבוֹת וְהוּא כְּנַחֲלָה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ הֶפְסֵק (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יב:) שֶׁהוּא חוּט הַמְשׁוּלָּשׁ.

— It is written, “You will give truth to Jacob,” and “the lip of truth will be established forever.” Hence “Jacob is the cord of His inheritance”: he encompasses all three patriarchal sanctities and is like an inheritance that never ends (as stated in Rosh Hashanah 12b), a threefold cord.

וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה אָמְרוּ (מְנָחוֹת מג:) כָּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ תְּפִילִּין וְכוּלֵי וְצִיצִית בְּבִגְדוֹ וּמְזוּזָה בְּפִתְחוֹ הַכֹּל בְּחִיזּוּק שֶׁלֹּא יֶחֱטָא שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְהַחוּט הַמְשׁוּלָּשׁ וְגוֹמֵר.

— Similarly, they taught that anyone who has tefillin, and so forth, tzitzit on his garment, and a mezuzah at his doorway is firmly protected against sin, as it says, “the threefold cord,” and so forth (Menachot 43b).

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 11:3: “Jacob our father, peace be upon him, was the mean between the holiness of the two Patriarchs, joining them together, and through this he attained the aspect of truth, the threefold cord that is not broken, for ‘the lip of truth will be established forever.’ The aspect of Abraham and Isaac was only that of faith: although they had revelations of Godliness, as it says, ‘Hashem appeared,’ these were only for a time, and all their days they held fast to their faith. … But of Jacob it is written, ‘God went up from him in the place where He had spoken with him,’ and Rashi says, ‘I do not know what this teaches us.’ Its plain intent is to make known Jacob’s distinction: even after the withdrawal, his soul remained in the same state as in the place where He spoke with him. This is the appearance of truth in him, and ‘the lip of truth will be established forever.’ This is the allusion: through lighting the Chanukah lamp, paired with the mezuzah on the right, which is the holiness of the two Patriarchs Abraham and Isaac, the thread of tzitzis in the middle becomes threefold, so that the threefold holiness of Jacob, the middle line that joins them, is fixed in us, to be ‘the cord of His inheritance.’”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Rav Tzadok again identifies Jacob, who joins Abraham and Isaac, with the threefold cord and with “the lip of truth established forever.” Here he explains why Jacob’s level endures, since his revelation remained after it withdrew, and ties the threefold cord to the Chanukah lamp, the mezuzah and the tzitzis.

p: וְכֵן כָּאן קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת עַצְמוֹ אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב׳ רד א) שִׁי״ן רָזָא דִּתְלָתָא אֲבָהָן דְּמִתְאַחֲדָן בְּבַת יְחִידָה וְאִיהִי מִתְעַטְּרָא בְּהוּ,
— Likewise, concerning the sanctity of Shabbat itself, the holy Zohar (II, 204a) teaches: “Shin is the mystery of the three patriarchs, who unite in the only daughter, and she is crowned with them.”
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַיִּשְׂרָאֵל זוֹכֶה בְּשַׁבָּת לִקְדוּשַּׁת שְׁלֹשֶׁת הָאָבוֹת וְהַיְינוּ בְּשָׁלֹשׁ סְעֻדּוֹת שַׁבָּת שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הָאָבוֹת.
— On Shabbat a Jew attains the sanctity of the three patriarchs, through the three Shabbat meals corresponding to them.

וְלָכֵן בְּמִנְחַת שַׁבָּת שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב שֶׁגַּם שָׁלֹשׁ הַתְּפִלּוֹת נֶגֶד הָאָבוֹת (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּקּוּן יח) אוֹמְרִים בְּמִנְחָה וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּתִי וְגוֹמֵר עֲנֵנִי בֶּאֱמֶת יִשְׁעֶךָ,

— Thus at Shabbat Minchah, corresponding to Jacob—for the three prayers too correspond to the patriarchs (as stated in Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 18)—we say, “As for me, my prayer,” and so forth, “answer me with the truth of Your salvation.”
שֶׁאָז זוֹכֶה הַיִּשְׂרָאֵל לִקְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב שְׂפַת אֱמֶת דְּתִכּוֹן לָעַד וּמְבַקְּשִׁים שֶׁתִּהְיֶה הַיְשׁוּעָה מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע וּמִכָּל רַע לָעַד.
— Then a Jew attains Jacob’s sanctity, the truthful lip established forever, and we ask that deliverance from the evil inclination and all evil endure forever.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 204a (Vayakhel 13:180): “What is Shabbat? If you say it is because of cessation, as it says, “For on it He ceased,” that is correct. But the mystery is this: when this point ascends and the light shines, it is crowned with the Patriarchs. Once crowned with them, it joins and unites with them as one, and all is called Shabbat: shin–bat. Shin, as has been explained, is the mystery of the three Patriarchs, who unite with the only daughter. She is crowned with them, and they with the World to Come; all is one. This is shin–bat: that all should be one.”

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 18, 34a–b: “There are three prayers on Shabbat, and the fourth is Musaf. The evening prayer is “You sanctified”: this is the lower Shekhinah, which belongs to the left side, where the Levites are, of whom it is said, “You shall sanctify the Levites.” The morning prayer is “Moses rejoices in the gift of his portion”: this is “The soul of every living being,” the supernal Mother, of whom it is said, “If you lie among the sheepfolds”—read not im, “if,” but em, “Mother.” Of her it is said, “He lay down in that place”: she lies in the place of the twenty-two letters of Torah. Fortunate is the mouth of Torah in which she rests at that hour. The third prayer is “You are One and Your Name is One”: this is the Lord, the middle pillar, which holds both together. These are the additional neshamah, ruach, and nefesh: additional nefesh on Shabbat eve, “You sanctified”; additional neshamah, “The soul of every living being,” of which it says “Moses rejoices in the gift of his portion”; additional ruach, “You are One and Your Name is One.” Fortunate is one who opens his mouth in the three prayers to receive them on Shabbat. Musaf is the righteous one who encompasses all the prayers, and in it we say, “A crown they shall give You, Lord our God.””

The evening prayer is “You sanctified”: this is the lower Shekhinah, which belongs to the left side, where the Levites are, of whom it is said, “You shall sanctify the Levites.” The morning prayer is “Moses rejoices in the gift of his portion”: this is “The soul of every living being,” the supernal Mother, of whom it is said, “If you lie among the sheepfolds”—read not im, “if,” but em, “Mother.” Of her it is said, “He lay down in that place”: she lies in the place of the twenty-two letters of Torah. Fortunate is the mouth of Torah in which she rests at that hour. The third prayer is “You are One and Your Name is One”: this is the Lord, the middle pillar, which holds both together. These are the additional neshamah, ruach, and nefesh: additional nefesh on Shabbat eve, “You sanctified”; additional neshamah, “The soul of every living being,” of which it says “Moses rejoices in the gift of his portion”; additional ruach, “You are One and Your Name is One.” Fortunate is one who opens his mouth in the three prayers to receive them on Shabbat. Musaf is the righteous one who encompasses all the prayers, and in it we say, “A crown they shall give You, Lord our God.””

p: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּבַקְּשִׁים בְּהַבְדָּלָה בִּתְפִלָּה עַל יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁנִּהְיֶה חֲשׂוּכִים מִכָּל חֵטְא וּמְנוּקִּים מִכָּל עָוֹן וּמְדוּבָּקִים בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ,
— As we request in Havdalah within the prayer concerning the weekdays: that we be held back from every sin, cleansed of every iniquity, and attached to fear of You.
שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת נִקְרְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל יִרְאֵי שְׁמִי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תַּעֲנִית ח:) וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שֶׁזּוֹכִין לִקְדוּשַּׁת הָאָבוֹת.
— On Shabbat Israel is called “those who fear My Name,” as stated in Taanit 8b, by virtue of attaining the patriarchs’ sanctity.
וּבְחִינַת הַיִּרְאָה מָצִינוּ בְּכָל הָאָבוֹת שֶׁבְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כְּתִיב עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה.
— We find awe in all the patriarchs. Of Abraham our father, peace be upon him, it is written, “Now I know that you fear God.”
וְיִצְחָק מִדָּתוֹ הַיִּרְאָה פַּחַד יִצְחָק כַּיָּדוּעַ וְיַעֲקֹב מִדָּתוֹ הַנּוֹרָא (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב׳ עט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א׳) וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁנּוֹפֵל פַּחַד הַשֵּׁם מִמֵּילָא.
— Isaac’s attribute is awe, “the Fear of Isaac,” as is known; Jacob’s is “the awesome” (as stated in Zohar II, 79a, beginning), so that fear of Hashem descends of itself.
וּמְבַקְּשִׁים עַל יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁנִּהְיֶה גַּם כֵּן מְדוּבָּקִים בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ וְלִהְיוֹת גִּבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ.
— We ask that during the weekdays too we remain attached to fear of You, becoming mighty by conquering our inclination.
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְהִקְדִּישׁוּ אֶת קְדוֹשׁ יַעֲקֹב.
— The root of holiness is Jacob’s aspect, as it says, “They shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob.”

h: Uniting Shabbat Chanukah and Rosh Chodesh

p: וּכְשֶׁחָל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ בְּשַׁבָּת חֲנוּכָּה הִיא קְדוּשָּׁה מְשׁוּלֶּשֶׁת דְּשַׁבָּת מְפוֹרָשׁ בֵּיהּ קְדוּשָּׁה דִּכְתִיב לָדַעַת כִּי אֲנִי הַשֵּׁם מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם וְהַיְינוּ קוֹדֶשׁ עִלָּאָה.
— When Rosh Chodesh falls on Shabbat Chanukah, the holiness is threefold. Shabbat is explicitly called holy: “To know that I, Hashem, sanctify you,” the supernal holiness.
וּבַחֹדֶשׁ גַּם כֵּן מָצִינוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כ.) הַחוֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה וְגוֹמֵר כָּזֶה רְאֵה וְקַדֵּשׁ.
— Concerning the month too we find, “‘This month,’ and so forth—see it like this and sanctify it” (Rosh Hashanah 20a).
וְכֵן (שָׁם כד.) רֹאשׁ בֵּית דִּין אוֹמֵר מְקוּדָּשׁ וְכָל הָעָם עוֹנִין אַחֲרָיו מְקוּדָּשׁ מְקוּדָּשׁ וְהַיְינוּ דְּנָהִיר לָהּ שִׁמְשָׁא מִקּוֹדֶשׁ עִלָּאָה.
— Likewise, the head of the court says “Sanctified,” and all the people answer, “Sanctified, sanctified” (ibid. 24a): the sun illuminates the moon from the supernal holiness.
וְכֵן חֲנוּכָּה שֶׁזּוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי הַנֵּרוֹת לְהַקְּדוּשָּׁה מֵאוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן וְהַחוּט הַמְשׁוּלָּשׁ בִּקְדוּשָּׁה מְשׁוּלֶּשֶׁת יָכוֹל לִפְעוֹל לְהַכְנִיס אוֹר וּקְדוּשָּׁה לִימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
— On Chanukah too, through the lamps one attains holiness from the primordial light. This threefold cord of threefold sanctity can bring light and holiness into the weekdays.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 20a: “Rabbah bar Shmuel taught: Might one think that just as a year is intercalated when necessary, a month is likewise extended when necessary? Scripture says, “This month shall be for you”—see it like this and sanctify it. Rava said: There is no difficulty. One case concerns extending the month, the other sanctifying it. The teaching means: Might one think that just as a year and a month are extended when necessary, the month may also be sanctified early when necessary? Scripture says, “This month shall be for you”—see it like this and sanctify it.”

paragraphs.text: Rosh Hashanah 24a: “The head of the court says, “Sanctified,” and all the people respond, “Sanctified, sanctified.” Whether the new moon was seen at its proper time or later, they sanctify the month. Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says: If it was not seen at its proper time, they do not sanctify it, because Heaven has already sanctified it. The Gemara asks: From where is the head of the court’s declaration derived? Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said in Rabbi Yose ben Shaul’s name, in Rabbi’s name: Scripture says, “Moses declared the appointed times of the Lord”; this teaches that the head of the court says, “Sanctified.” From where is the people’s response derived? Rav Pappa said: “Which you shall proclaim”—read it as “you yourselves.” Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: “These are My appointed times”—they shall declare My appointed times. Why say “Sanctified” twice? Because it is written, “Holy convocations,” in the plural.”
